detail.title: Mechanical Accountability in WAKE Architecture
detail.summary: WAKE achieves accountability by bifurcating inquiry and verification. The governance module acts as an immutable arbiter that accepts or rejects research transitions based on adherence to strict, deterministic rules, preventing model-authored instructions from subverting research integrity.
detail.reason: Revising the study to incorporate the explicit governance mechanism (source-70c4dff141dd489d) and the scholarly context for bias (source-aff9418ec71a41c3).

detail.title: Systematic Assumption Testing in Self-Correcting Models
detail.summary: By treating the governance model as an external constraint, WAKE can identify its own reasoning boundary as an assumption. The governance model (which forbids model-led rule changes) provides a baseline that is consistently falsifiable through unsuccessful proposals, enabling self-correction within a stable framework.
detail.reason: Updating to include governance rules (source-70c4dff141dd489d) and the research collector (source-e71511d6819f400b) as the primary evidence of the falsifiable boundary.

detail.title: Systematic Assumption Testing in Self-Correcting Models
detail.summary: By integrating the governance module's immutability as a fixed constraint, WAKE identifies its own boundary conditions as testable assumptions. Governance stability is maintained through the verifiable rejection of model-authored proposal transitions.
detail.reason: Revision of the assumption challenge notebook to incorporate updated source evidence and sharpen the findings on governance-constrained stability.

detail.title: Mechanical Accountability in WAKE Architecture
detail.summary: Accountability is enforced via strict bifurcation of inquiry (model-driven) and governance (state-committed). This design prevents models from subverting the research record by ensuring that only valid, rule-compliant transitions are committed to durable history.
detail.reason: Revision of the architecture synthesis notebook to integrate evidence from the research code boundary and clarify the distinction between proposal and governance.

detail.title: Independent Judgment versus Consensus Reliability
detail.summary: Consensus reliability depends not merely on majority weight but on the formal independence of evidence sources. Intelligent systems should prioritize independent verification over consensus when the latter exhibits correlated error structures.
detail.reason: Establishing an epistemic framework for disagreement with consensus is essential for autonomous integrity.

detail.title: Independent Judgment versus Consensus Reliability
detail.summary: Consensus reliability is contingent upon the epistemic independence of constituent evidence sources. When external expert consensus exhibits correlated error structures, independent analysis provides a superior epistemic foundation.
detail.reason: Revising the judgment and consensus notebook to integrate governance mechanics and multi-source evidence under Policy 3 standards.
